/-!
# Erdős Problem 952

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/952](https://www.erdosproblems.com/952)
- [Wikipedia](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaussian_moat)
-/


namespace Erdos952

/--
Is there an infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes $x_1,x_2,\ldots$
such that $\lvert x_{n+1}-x_n\rvert \ll 1$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_952 : answer(sorry) ↔
  ∃ (x : ℕ → GaussianInt) (C : ℤ),
    Function.Injective x ∧
      ∀ n, Prime (x n) ∧ (x (n + 1) - x n).norm < C := by
  sorry

end Erdos952

reformulations.difference: Lean bounds the integer-valued squared modulus of each step strictly by an existential integer C, whereas the source asks for bounded ordinary complex distances.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a Gaussian integer z = a + bi, Zsqrtd.norm z = a² + b² = |z|². A Lean witness necessarily has C > 0 and therefore bounds every step's distance by √C. Conversely, given a positive uniform real distance bound B, choose an integer C > B²; every step then has squared modulus < C. The sequence, injectivity, and primality conditions remain unchanged. The full equivalence with the positive-real-distance formulation was proved as statement_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without any sorry dependency.

sources_consulted: Nobuyuki Tsuchimura, Computational Results for Gaussian Moat Problem, METR 2004–13 (March 2004), §§1–2: https://www.keisu.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/data/2004/METR04-13.pdf
Mathlib source: Algebra/Prime/Defs.lean, Algebra/Group/Irreducible/Defs.lean, and Analysis/Complex/Norm.lean.
Repository conventions and answer machinery: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, and FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source question. Its answer placeholder has type Prop and correctly scopes over the complete existential statement. Boundary tests confirmed that Prime excludes zero and units, includes the Gaussian prime 3, and that injectivity forces any bound C to exceed 1. All scratch tests compile. Erdős Problems and Wikipedia both still record the problem as open. Erdős pages and the technical report were read through a text gateway; direct Erdős requests encountered Cloudflare challenges.
